w1_1a: Every morning, start here. The app reads all your deals and puts what needs you at the top.
w1_1b: Tap it done and the right people are told. Not today? Push it — it comes back tomorrow.
w1_2a: Under your tasks is a short call list, picked for you each morning, with the reason to call.
w1_2b: Work it top to bottom. When the list is done, the day is won.
w1_3a: Every deal you're working, as cards.
w1_3b: Read All shows what's live; use the dropdown for on-hold or closed. Tap any card to open it.
w1_4a: Calendar shows every deadline from every deal on one page.
w1_4b: And if something's yours alone — pick up a lockbox, drop off a gift — add a task and it shows up on Win The Day like everything else.
w2_1a: Have a signed contract? Don't type it.
w2_1b: Upload it — the app reads the price, the dates, the deposits and everyone's contact info, and builds the whole timeline in under a minute.
w2_2a: No contract yet? New Deal is three questions: the address, your client, the price.
w2_2b: The timeline, the checklist and the client emails build themselves.
w2_3a: Text a new buyer or seller your intake link.
w2_3b: They answer a few questions on their phone, and a lead lands on your deals list — flagged so you call them within the day.
w2_4a: Going on a listing appointment? Price the home first, right here — no deal needed.
w2_4b: If you win it, one tap turns the CMA into the deal.
w3_1a: Every deal opens on its Overview, and the one line that matters is at the top: the next step.
w3_1b: You don't have to remember the timeline. The app does. Your job is just the next step.
w3_2a: The Timeline is every step from here to closing, with its date. Mark a step done when it's done.
w3_2b: Appointments ask for a date and time — and then remind everyone who needs to be there.
w3_3a: Every paper on the deal, in one place. Drag a file in and it files itself. The checklist at the top tells you what's still missing for a clean file.
w3_3b: Share sends a document to your client, in your name, and it appears in their portal.
w3_4a: Need a signature? Tap Get signature, pick who, send. They sign on their phone.
w3_4b: The signed copy files itself back here with a certificate — no DocuSign, and if they stall, the app chases them for you.
w3_5a: Everyone on the deal goes here — your client, the other agent, the lender, title, the inspector.
w3_5b: Add them once. Welcome emails go out in your name, and you see every one before it sends.
w3_6a: Your buyer or seller gets their own private page: where the deal stands, what's needed from them, what happens next, and you one tap away.
w3_6b: It's most of the calls you take in a week, answered before they call.
w3_7a: Message anyone on the deal from here — email, text, or both, in one send.

w4_1a: Answer four questions — price, deposit, financing, closing — and the app fills the official Florida contract with the right riders.
w4_1b: Need to change a term? Every field is right there. Then send it for signature without leaving the page.
w4_2a: When an offer comes in, upload it. The app reads it and parks it as pending — nothing sends yet. Two offers?
w4_2b: Your seller compares them side by side in their portal. Approve the winner and the deal goes under contract with its timeline built.
w4_3b: The listing package fills the official forms from what the deal already knows — brokerage, commission, term, your license — and drops them into Documents ready to sign.
w4_4a: Dates changed in an addendum? Tap Read dates on any document.
w4_4b: The app finds the new dates, shows you what moved, and updates the timeline when you say so.
w4_5a: Deals fall apart. Choose Contract fell through and the app archives everything for your file, clears the other side, and puts the listing back on the market with a fresh timeline.
w4_6a: If your buyer waives the inspection, one tap makes the release — it records that you recommended one and they declined — and sends it for signature.

w5_4a: Scripts give you the words for the hard conversations. Vendors lets you hand a client your trusted plumber in one tap.
